title: Laying Plans
coreMove: Run the five-factor comparison before action so you know whether the field can support the move you want to make.
sourcePressure: The opening frames war as a life-or-ruin inquiry governed by five constant factors, seven comparative questions, adaptation to circumstance, deception, and many calculations before battle.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating planning as motivational goal-setting or a generic pros-and-cons list.

sourceAnchors.name: the five constant factors
sourceAnchors.detail: Moral Law, Heaven, Earth, the Commander, and Method and discipline are named as the heads to compare before action.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Before the first move, lay the five factors side by side until the ground itself starts arguing for or against the plan.

sourceAnchors.name: the temple calculations
sourceAnchors.detail: The winner is described as making many calculations before battle while the loser makes few or none.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The battle is often decided in the quiet room where the calculations happen before anyone moves.

hook: A battlefield metaphor imported into a modern office before the actual choice is visible
A generic sentence about strategy being planning under pressure
counterintuition: The obvious move is not always best; the opposite move is smarter
Winning is not about strength but about strategy
tryThisNow: Set a timer and think about your next battle
Write down your goal and one obstacle
examples: manager staring at a spreadsheet with a coffee cup

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches repeated phrases but not the deeper template of timestamp plus named protagonist plus prop plus decision that makes six examples feel like one example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a direct question, a tactical aside, a second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence

exampleSpecs.domain: hospital winter staffing triage after three nurses call in sick
exampleSpecs.audience: operations lead in a regional hospital
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the emergency department opens four beds safely during a flu spike
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sarah writes five headings on the glass board, puts staffing, weather, patient flow, charge nurse authority, and supply routes under them, then cancels the bed-opening plan when Earth and Method fail.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a glove dispenser with a handwritten out-of-stock tag

exampleSpecs.domain: commercial bakery deciding whether to accept a supermarket rush order
exampleSpecs.stakes: a contract could double revenue but break delivery reliability
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It took Thomas one rejected pallet to see that he had counted ovens and ignored loading-bay distance.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: six cracked baguette trays beside the loading door

exampleSpecs.domain: municipal flood-response drill before spring melt
exampleSpecs.stakes: a riverside district may need evacuation within six hours
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The river gauge blinks amber while Camille compares road access, night temperature, radio coverage, public trust, and command authority before approving the drill route.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an amber river gauge above wet concrete steps

exampleSpecs.domain: shipping-line reroute around a port strike
exampleSpecs.stakes: salmon containers will spoil if the alternate route lacks cold-chain discipline
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Cold vapor rolls from a cracked reefer door as Henrik separates favorable opportunity from missing method and discipline.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: cold vapor from a reefer container

exampleSpecs.domain: museum deciding whether to move a fragile exhibit before a donor gala
exampleSpecs.stakes: a rushed move could damage a seventeenth-century cabinet
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show me the route, not the guest list, Sofia says, then walks the corridor measuring door widths before approving any promise to the director.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a tape measure across a marble doorway

exampleSpecs.domain: cybersecurity team weighing public disclosure after a vendor breach
exampleSpecs.audience: security lead at a Toronto software firm
exampleSpecs.stakes: early disclosure could protect clients or trigger avoidable panic
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: What changes if the adversary already knows the gap and the clients do not?
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a redacted vendor incident email on a laptop
mustAvoid: abstract risk matrix with no action

skillTargets: choose when five-factor comparison should precede action
distinguish adaptation from abandoning the plan
identify deception as positioning, not lying for its own sake

tryThisNowSpec: Before your next consequential move, score the five factors on one page and circle the factor that would make the plan fail even if your willpower held.
